I flinch for a moment, but stand firm. Because I decided to face her with everything I have.
...Her profile and the look in her eyes that I watched all day today flash back to me.

You do your job. I thoroughly carry out mine.
...I only think that is how things should be.

And finally. When my legs have begun to feel rather—
no, immensely heavy, I at last realize.
Huh...? To see Grandpa?

I manage to wave a hand and say I'm fine, then state it clearly.
What Believe had been stopping to gaze at all along was—
Huh...?

In such things...
dwells the work of true artisans.

And above all else,
because of her unwavering, earnest devotion to "craft"—
Fast...
Like Grandpa. ...The very best, finest work.

So that no matter what happens, no matter what comes, it will endure.
So that it can continue fulfilling the role expected of it to the fullest.

Just following behind me as I walk.
—Is that really fine with you?

It brings me back to my starting line.
My origin.
...Heading to the next job. ...Coming along?
...Yes.
Well—fast is always the best.
Oho. ...Wanna watch too?
...Just—buildings that have stood for a very long time.

Still, as I stand beside her, staring quietly at an old building that
bore the weight of years, waiting, waiting, and waiting... eventually—

This is Believe's precious origin.
A deep, heartfelt understanding firmly connects everything that has happened so far.

What did the young Believe look at with those earnest eyes? What did she yearn for?
I will never know the most vital part unless I see it for myself!

! ...Yeah.
I wanna see. ...Grandpa's work.

Grandpa.
...Are you watching the races today too?
...You came over today too, huh.

No... um, that's going to be difficult.
Grandpa is an exceptionally skilled craftsman—
To achieve that, first—

Yeah. ...I wonder who's gonna win?
Hey, Grandpa.

From long ago.
Enduring the wind, the rain... the harshness of time, standing right here.

Huh?
...Um, aren't you exhausted? ...Are you alright?

...Um.
Well then, I will be going.
Just when I think that, she comes to a dead stop.

Through thoroughly forged fundamentals and impeccably refined technique,
accomplished to perfection... first-class craftsmanship.

Recognized for his skills, he's currently... invited to work in America.
Going to see him would be tough—

No, not particularly.
Even with previous trainers, it was never like that.

A smile naturally forms on my face now that I've finally touched her true feelings.
With that, I add, "However—"

...My grandfather was.
A skilled plasterer, and—

That is why I want to know more. And I want to support it.
The path toward the dream Believe truly wishes to walk.

...Respect, or rather.
It's nothing so grand—

(The gentle breeze drifting in from the veranda. A tiny, well-worn TV.
The sweet fragrance of the pears Grandma peeled for me.)

Yeah. ...Same as my work.
Fast is always the best.

Indeed, simply "setting the menu and leaving the running to the girl"
isn't the sole job of a Trainer. In short, she needs—

(...I remember. What I admired. My origin.
The silent, solemn, dignified back I used to look up to without a word.)

Believe respected the "Trainer's" job and simply followed orders in silence.
Yet deep within her heart, I now understand she holds a precious dream.
Ah—

And so, Believe began walking.
Pacing forward steadily, we first reached town—

Continuing on, we arrived at the shopping street near the academy.
...What Believe did there was the exact same as before.

(The brick house... is already done.
It's so, ...so pretty.)
...The work of a master craftsman—
Wait... what? ...Huh...!?

Believe fell silent.
It took a long, long time before she opened her mouth again.
I want to do good work, too.

Our strange journey continues in silence. Time drifts by leisurely,
at a walking pace, as I gaze at her swaying back ahead of me.

That sense of responsibility when she repaired the hearth all on her own.
And how, despite her few words, she said, "I want to be fast. That matters most."
